A module "such an object could be" is one your code passes around as a value or binds to another name (m = ops), gets by name (importlib.import_module, sys.modules, a string naming it), or one pytest hands out (test modules, conftests). A name bound only to modules (m = ops, then m.value()) is followed like the import itself.

An instance attribute is followed only when every assignment of it is in __init__ and assigns a parameter, a string, or one of your functions or classes by name. An attribute that holds an object (self.client = Client()) is not typed for calls: self.client.get() is matched against every method named get.

Dynamic lookups are bounded by imports, if at all.

A function that uses eval, exec, globals(), vars() or getattr with a computed name is treated as affected by any change in the modules its module imports, and in the modules of code that stores objects on one of those modules. Some code changes that bound:

  • Lookups on a library module. getattr(logging, name) is bounded unless your code may store something on that module: directly, by handing the module to other code, or by putting an object in sys.modules under its name. Then any change can affect the lookup. A patch undone when the test ends doesn't count (see Patches in tests below).
  • Lookup tables. A name taken from a dict, list or set written in the code (getattr(handlers, NAMES[key]), the export table of a lazy __getattr__) is bounded by that table only while nothing can change it. Once the table, or the module holding it, is modified, passed to other code, or reached through globals(), vars(), sys.modules or exec, the lookup counts as dynamic. A parameter or local variable that happens to share the table's name isn't bounded by it.
  • Names in strings. operator.attrgetter("a.b"), methodcaller("m"), a format template's fields ("{0.name}") and a match class pattern (case C(x=1), or case C(1) through __match_args__) read attributes by name. They are matched like getattr(x, "a"). A name or template that isn't written out is bounded by what callers pass, or else counts as dynamic.
  • Names that start with fixed text. f"plugins.{name}" is bounded to the modules it can name.
Code loaded at run time can be affected by any change.

These can reach any of your code, so the code using them is selected for any change:

  • a module imported or run by a name nothing bounds (importlib.import_module(name), runpy.run_module(name), runpy.run_path(path));
  • a module loaded from a file whose path is computed (importlib.util.spec_from_file_location);
  • an object unpickled from data the code doesn't write out. A pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(x)) round trip, and bytes written in the code, are followed.
Modules obtained at run time count as any of your modules.

A module your code gets by a name it computes counts as any of your modules, so passing it on or writing to it makes every lookup table dynamic. The same goes for a function's __globals__, a frame's f_globals, and what pickle.loads, pkgutil.resolve_name or gc.get_objects() hand back.

Two exceptions: a name that starts with fixed text, and a new module (types.ModuleType(name)) that isn't installed in sys.modules under a name of yours. A copy made with importlib.util.module_from_spec counts as the module whose file it loads.

Replacing a module in sys.modules reaches every importer. Code that puts an object in sys.modules for good under a computed name may replace any of your modules. Without a recording, every test that imports one of them depends on that code.

items.title: Objects and modules handed to other code
items.text: Passing a module on depends on all of it. Code that passes a module to other code (read(ops, name)) depends on everything in that module and on what its imports bind (api.core.TABLE). That holds whether the module is named by an import or obtained with importlib.import_module("pkg.sub"). Passing an object on depends on all of its methods. Code that hands an instance of one of your classes to other code depends on every method of that class, since the receiving code may call any of them by name. That covers a library (json.dump(x, w), csv.writer(w), print(file=w), dict(obj), handler.stream = w), a method on an object of unknown type (items.append(w)), and your own functions. Builtins that only use dunder methods (len, str, iter, sorted) don't count.

items.title: Code a test runs from text or in another process
items.text:
Text run as code. exec, eval, timeit and pytest's pytester.makepyfile run text. Text written in the code (a string, a constant, a template filled with literals) is read as code: what it imports and calls counts. Text built at run time or read from a file can import anything, so the test is selected for any change. Text passed in as a helper's argument is read at each call site. A template filled by the test's own argument is read once per value when @pytest.mark.parametrize on the test function lists literal values for it (and the test has no decorator other than pytest marks); values from a fixture, indirect=True, or a parametrize on the class or in pytestmark count as built at run time. Tests that use pytester. A test using pytester or testdir runs a pytest session of its own, with your project's registered plugins loaded. It depends on every fixture those plugins define, and on what its inline test code imports. Python programs a test starts.

A test that runs a script or module of your project in a new process depends on that program and on what it imports, when the code names it in a string: [sys.executable, "scripts/gen.py"], python -m mypkg.tool, python -c "import mypkg". This also works after env X=1, uv run or timeout 30, and with asyncio.create_subprocess_exec.

  • A test file given to a test runner (python -m pytest tests/test_x.py, pytest.main([...]), python -m unittest tests.cases) runs whole: the test depends on everything in that file and its conftest.py files.
  • A .py file no module name maps to (scripts/gen-data.py) is read like -c code: the test depends on the file and on what it imports.
  • When the program is built at run time, the test is selected for any change: a path from a variable or the environment, -c code assembled from pieces, a program that imports by a computed name or changes sys.path, *args, a directory, or unittest discover.
  • Console scripts your project installs and files outside your source roots aren't seen.

Execution evidence follows the processes a test starts.

items.title: State shared between tests
items.text:
State changed in place reaches every reader.

Code that changes a module-level object, directly or by handing it to a function that changes it (register(REGISTRY), registry.add(x)), is a dependency of every reader of that object. A change to a function also reaches the readers of whatever the functions it calls change in place.

Not followed:

  • an object stored away and changed later under another name (self.store = store, then self.store[k] = v);
  • an object a function returns that its caller then changes;
  • a library function that changes an argument you pass it, a module of yours included (a library writing into a module you hand it).
Patches in tests.

A store on a module, yours or a library's, makes the code storing a dependency of every reader. A patch undone when the test ends doesn't count:

  • a method of pytest's monkeypatch or pytest-mock's mocker, called in the test or in a function-scoped fixture that requests it, unless that module defines its own fixture of the same name;
  • a with mock.patch(...) or with MonkeyPatch.context() block in a function that doesn't yield;
  • a @mock.patch(...) decorator;
  • a value saved and put back in a test or a function-scoped fixture: orig = m.X, then m.X = v, restored in a finally: block or, in a fixture, right after the yield.

Any other patch counts as a store that may outlast the test: patch(...).start(), a patcher kept for later, a MonkeyPatch() of your own, monkeypatch handed to a helper function, a with mock.patch(...) around a yield in a fixture, or a monkeypatch fixture the same module overrides.

An override of monkeypatch or mocker in a parent conftest.py is not seen: diffcone still assumes what a test patches through it is undone when the test ends.

Tests are assumed not to depend on what an earlier test left behind.

When code that runs inside one test changes module state (server._state = make()), diffcone counts that change for that test only, not for other tests that read the same state. Such code is:

  • the test itself, and unittest's setUp and tearDown;
  • a function-scoped fixture;
  • a helper in a test module or conftest.py that only such code calls.

A test or setUp that other code calls (a test module's top-level code, a session fixture) is not such code, and neither is a doctest's function. Code that runs once for many tests is a dependency of every test that reads what it changes: a test module's top-level code, a fixture with a wider scope (or a scope it computes), a hook, and any code of your project, a cache it fills included.

If a test relies on state an earlier test set up, declare that dependency in diffcone.toml (an [[edges]] entry from the reader to the code setting it up), or run the whole suite.

Caches with a recording.

With a recording, a test that reads a cache an earlier test filled counts as running the code that filled it. That works when your code fills the cache with a value it computes, itself or through a helper it hands the value to (_put(key, compute(key))), and keeps it in a module variable, on an object or class, in a closure or a function attribute, or behind a memoising decorator. A decorator's registration (@router.get("/path")) doesn't count as filling a cache, and neither does a literal written into a module variable before the code has run anything else.

A decorator counts as memoising when diffcone knows it (functools, cachetools, Django's and Werkzeug's cached_property, and others) or its name says so (cached_property, cached, memoize, memoized, cachedmethod).

Not followed:

  • a cache kept by an installed package's decorator under another name;
  • a cache filled through a method of an object whose type diffcone can't tell (self._cache.set(k, compute(k)) where _cache is set in several ways);
  • a cache filled with an attribute of the object the code runs on (_CACHE[key] = self.result) that other code computed.
Code that changes the process while pytest collects reaches every test. A conftest.py, a test module or a module they import may set an environment variable, extend sys.path or configure a library (warnings.filterwarnings, logging.basicConfig) when it's imported. A collection hook may do the same. That can change what any later test sees, so such code is a dependency of every test. Static discovery lists what is recognised. With a recording, code run while pytest collects a file reaches that file's tests. Building parameter ids, an ids= function and pytest_generate_tests decide the tests of the file pytest is collecting, so a change there selects that file's tests and whoever reads what the code stored. Code that pytest hands its objects to can also leave something for hooks that act on every test. That is recognised when the code, or what ran it, reads .config, .session, .stash or .pluginmanager, or is a hook other than pytest_generate_tests, and then every test is selected. Something left on another pytest object (metafunc.function, a node's attributes) for a later hook to act on is not.

items.title: Reading files
items.text:
A file that doesn't parse selects everything. Any .py file under your source roots that isn't valid Python 3, or can't be decoded in its declared encoding (UTF-8 unless the file says otherwise), is an analysis error, even a test data file nothing imports. So is one that nests an expression hundreds of levels deep, as generated code may (a sum of a thousand terms). Choose source roots that leave such files out. Uncommitted analysis is only as stable as your working tree. A plan of WORKTREE or INDEX describes the files at the moment you planned. The report always marks such plans as uncommitted. Git-ignored files are seen only by WORKTREE plans, and only Python ones.

A plan of a commit or of INDEX reads what git recorded. A .py file git ignores (a generated _version.py, a local_settings.py) and any edit to it are invisible to it. run refuses to run such a plan while one is on disk under your source roots: plan with --head WORKTREE instead.

A WORKTREE plan reads ignored .py files in a directory that also holds files git tracks or doesn't ignore. A directory with only ignored files is skipped, as are ignored directories (a virtualenv, a build tree) and ignored files that aren't Python.

items.title: Discovery
items.text: Discovery reads the source, so it can't see what plugins do. A pytest plugin that collects tests by its own rules, or a test base class outside your source roots, can mean diffcone's target list is incomplete. diffcone reports it and the plan exits with code 3 (static discovery). A plugin that collects files just by being installed is invisible to a plan from the code. Whenever run starts pytest, it runs every collected test the plan doesn't know, and a recording captures what pytest really collected. Parametrized tests are selected as a whole. diffcone selects or skips all of a test's parameter cases together.

items.title: Execution evidence
items.text:
Reading the code works well when changes stay local. In a large library where nearly every module imports a few central ones, a change to a central module can reach nearly every test, so a plan selects nearly the whole suite.

Execution evidence fixes this. You record once which functions each test actually ran, and diffcone selects the tests whose recorded run touches the change.

Requirements

Recording needs Python 3.12 or later in your project's test environment. diffcone itself can run on another Python version.

items.title: Record
items.text:
From a clean checkout of a commit, run your suite under the recorder. Arguments after -- are passed to pytest. The examples use the default source root; for a src layout, add --source-root src --source-root . to every command here, collect included (a recording keeps its source roots, and plans must use the same ones):

diffcone collect --command "uv run pytest" -- -n 8

This writes a recording to .diffcone/evidence/: for each test, the functions it ran and the files it read. To record a different commit without checking it out, add --rev REV. diffcone evidence lists your recordings:

diffcone evidence

collect refuses to record a commit with a file it can't analyse, since the code in it couldn't be matched to what the tests ran. If pytest stops early (an interrupt, an internal error, a usage error), nothing is written.

Plans find each test's recording by its pytest node ID. If your repository has no pytest configuration and a directory above it has one, pytest takes that directory as its rootdir and every node ID starts with the path to your repository, so plans find no recording for any test. collect warns when none of the recorded tests matches a test it discovers; add --rootdir=. to the command, or give the repository a pytest configuration of its own.

A recording made by an earlier version of diffcone may not be readable by a later one. diffcone evidence and --evidence auto then skip it (so auto fails with "no evidence recording" if it was the only one), and naming its path is an error. Record again.

Some tests behave differently depending on what ran before them. Add --reverse-check to run the suite a second time in reverse order; tests whose recordings differ are marked unstable and always selected.

items.title: Plan with a recording
items.text:
diffcone plan --base main --head WORKTREE --discover pytest --evidence auto

--evidence auto uses the recording, made with the same source roots, from the nearest ancestor of the head (or pass a recording's path). The recording doesn't need to be at your base: diffcone also accounts for the changes made since it was recorded.

plan doesn't run anything, so it can't check that your test environment is the one the recording was made in: the report says environment NOT checked (environment_checked: false in JSON). Its selection holds only in the recorded environment. diffcone run checks it before any test runs (see below).

A test is selected when, in its recorded run, it:

  • ran a function that changed;
  • read a value or definition that changed;
  • looked up a name dynamically where something the lookup can see changed; or
  • read a file that changed.

It is also selected when its own code, class or module changed, when the fixtures, hooks or plugins around it changed, and when an [[always_run]] entry names it.

Some changes can't be judged from a recording, and diffcone says so in the report:

  • Code that runs when a module is imported is planned from the code, as without evidence. The exception is a changed constant or class attribute, which selects the tests that read it.
  • The recorder starts before pytest loads any plugin (-p in addopts, PYTEST_ADDOPTS or your command) and before your own sitecustomize.py, so what those import is recorded. If a module of your project was imported before that (by a .pth file, or under python -S), collect warns and lists it in preloaded_modules; changes to it are always planned from the code.
  • If one test fills a cache and later tests read it, every test that reads it counts. This covers caches in module variables, on objects and classes, in closures, in function attributes and in cached_property. functools.cache and lru_cache are cleared before each test instead. Caches kept by an unknown memoising decorator, or filled through a method of an object whose type diffcone can't tell, are not seen (see limitations).
  • Tests with no recording (new tests, for example), tests whose recording was unstable, and tests that failed or errored while they were recorded are always selected: a failing test's recording stops where it failed.

  • Processes a test starts:

    • Followed. A Python process started with subprocess (directly, through asyncio, or through uv run) records itself on Linux and macOS. The test is credited with what it ran, and so is every test that runs while it is still running.
    • Always selected. A test that starts a process any other way (os.system, a shell, multiprocessing, or anything on Windows), or whose child can't record itself. So is every test that runs while such a process is still running (a multiprocessing pool reused by a later test), and a test whose child runs your code from a python -c snippet or a script outside your source roots.
    • Ignored. A python -c snippet that can't run your code (a version check), and package-manager commands such as uv sync, uv pip or uv python list.

    A project sitecustomize.py still runs in every child. - A process started outside every test (by a conftest.py as it is imported, or in a hook) counts as part of that import or hook: a change to what it ran is planned as a change to code that ran there. One that can't be followed makes every change do so, which can select every test. - A test that runs code from text rather than a file (doctests, including pytest's --doctest-modules, timeit statements, a notebook kernel) is always selected: that code can use any name of your code. Annotations evaluated from text (string annotations, which pydantic and FastAPI evaluate) are not: the test is credited with the function or class they belong to and the classes and functions they name. - Code that background threads are running while a test runs is credited to that test. - Code that ran while pytest collected a test file (building the ids of parametrized tests, an ids= function, a pytest_generate_tests hook and what it calls) decides that file's tests: a change to it, or to what it reads, selects the tests of every file it ran for, and the tests reading anything it stored. So does a change to a file read then. It counts as a hook's (below) when what ran it, or what that can run, sets something for the whole process, such as an environment variable, or reaches pytest's configuration or session. - Code that ran outside every test in a pytest hook (pytest_configure, pytest_collection_modifyitems, the collection of a directory) can affect any test: a change to it, or to what it reads, selects every test, and so does a change to pytest_plugins. Reading a function's annotations there (as pytest does on Python 3.14) is not running the function: only a change to the annotations, or to what they name, counts. - Changes to compiled sources (except Cython with a profiled recording), build files, dependencies and configuration select every test. - On a file system that ignores case (macOS and Windows by default), a file a test opened under another spelling (Data/Expected.TXT) still counts as the file it is. A file read through a symlink, or a symlinked directory, counts as the file it really is as well as under the name it was opened by; a link a test reads with os.readlink is the link. - Files are recorded however a test reaches them: opened, stat'ed, listed, through a sqlite3 file: URI, through a directory descriptor (os.listdir(fd), dir_fd=, os.fstat) or as entries of a directory it scanned with os.scandir (os.walk, glob, pathlib): an edit to any file of a scanned directory selects the test. A descriptor the recorder cannot trace to a path makes the test always selected.

ASV benchmarks are always planned from the code.

items.title: Run with a recording
items.text:
diffcone run --base main --head HEAD --discover pytest \
    --command "uv run pytest" --evidence auto -- -n 8

A recording is only valid in the environment it was made in. Before any test runs, even when the plan selects nothing, run checks that these match the recording:

  • the Python implementation and version, and its -O setting;
  • the platform and machine;
  • the installed packages;
  • your PYTHONPATH;
  • a few environment variables (TZ, LANG, LC_ALL, PYTHONWARNINGS, VIRTUAL_ENV).

It sets PYTHONHASHSEED to the recorded value itself. With --dry-run, nothing is checked.

If the environment doesn't match, or the check couldn't run, run falls back to a plan from the code and tells you what differed. If that plan's discovery may be incomplete, it runs the whole suite instead, unless you pass --allow-incomplete-discovery.

A package installed in editable mode from outside your repository (pip install -e ../lib) counts as installed: diffcone doesn't see edits to its code, as with any other installed package. If your tests also depend on your own environment variables, record them with --env-var:

diffcone collect --command "uv run pytest" --env-var MYAPP_MODE -- -n 8

The environment is the one at the end of the recording. If your tests install or upgrade a package while they run (a test that runs uv sync or pip install with your test interpreter, for example), collect warns and names the packages: a fresh install from your lock file then never matches the recording, and every run falls back to a plan from the code. run says so too when it meets the environment the recording started in. Stop the tests from changing their own environment to use the recording.

items.title: Keep the recording current
items.text:
Recording the whole suite for every commit would be slow. With --collect, run records the tests it runs and writes a new recording for the head: fresh records for the tests it ran, and the earlier ones for the tests it didn't select, which behave the same at the head.

diffcone run --base main --head HEAD --discover pytest \
    --command "uv run pytest" --evidence auto --collect -- -n 8

This needs a clean checkout of the head, and the same --command, pytest arguments and source roots the recording was made with. If the recording was made with --reverse-check, run --collect runs the selected tests a second time in reverse order, so the new records are checked the same way.

If the environment differs, or pytest is interrupted or ends with an error of its own (not a test failure), no recording is written. A run stopped at a failure (-x) still writes one, and the tests it didn't reach are selected until they are recorded again.

In CI, a common setup records the full suite once a night on your default branch and plans each pull request from it. See CI.

items.title: Cython
items.text:
diffcone can also select tests for changes to Cython code (.pyx, .pxd, .pxi) when the recording was made with a build compiled with Cython's profile=True directive, on Python 3.13 or later. Your test runs can keep using your normal build.

With such a recording:

  • a change inside a Cython function selects the tests that ran it (or ran a function that calls it);
  • a change outside functions (an import, a constant, a declaration, a new function) selects the tests that ran code using the changed name.

Changes diffcone can't attribute to a name, such as a compiler directive or a C source file, select every test. diffcone doesn't build your project; you provide the profiled build for recording.

items.title: Shallow clones
items.text:
Planning needs the recorded commit to be present in git. In a shallow clone (common in CI), fetch it first; diffcone names the commit when it's missing:

git fetch --depth=1 origin <commit>

In a shallow clone, --evidence auto can't tell which commits are ancestors, so pass the recording's path instead.

items.title: Planning
items.text:
diffcone plan compares two snapshots and reports which targets the changes between them can affect. It reads files and git objects only: it doesn't check anything out, import your code, or run tests.

diffcone plan --base main --head HEAD --discover pytest \
    --source-root src --source-root . --format text

items.title: Choose what to compare
items.text:
--base and --head each take a git revision, INDEX or WORKTREE (snapshots). Common combinations:

You want to check Use Uncommitted work, before you commit --base HEAD --head WORKTREE A branch, before you open a pull request --base main --head WORKTREE A pull request in CI --base origin/main --head HEAD Only what you have staged --base HEAD --head INDEX

Git-ignored files

A plan of a commit sees only what git recorded. A .py file git ignores (a generated _version.py or _pb2.py, a local_settings.py) is invisible to it, and so is any change you make to one.

A WORKTREE plan reads such files, as new modules on top of the base commit, when their directory also holds files git tracks or doesn't ignore. A directory with only ignored files is skipped, as are ignored directories (a virtualenv, a build tree) and ignored data files.

If your tests depend on generated Python, plan against WORKTREE, or commit what they import.

items.title: Source roots
items.text:
A source root is a directory that diffcone treats as an import root, the way Python's sys.path does. Module names come from the closest root that contains a file:

Roots src/calc/ops.py tests/test_calc.py . (the default) src.calc.ops tests.test_calc src and . calc.ops tests.test_calc src and tests calc.ops test_calc

Use the roots your code is actually imported from. For a src layout, that's usually --source-root src --source-root .; for a flat layout, the default is fine. Files outside every root are not analysed, so code there is treated like a third-party library.

Under the roots, diffcone reads only .py files. A change to any other file there (a data file, a README.md) selects every target, since your code may read it. With the root ., that includes your documentation. See limitations for why, and execution evidence for a way to narrow it.

If one pytest session collects several test directories whose files share names (common in monorepos that use --import-mode=importlib), give each directory its own namespace with DIR=PREFIX:

diffcone plan --base main --head HEAD --discover pytest \
    --source-root packages/api/src --source-root packages/api/tests=api_tests

items.title: Discover them
items.text:
--discover pytest and --discover asv find targets by reading your configuration and test files, the way the runner would collect them, without importing anything. To see what discovery finds, write it to a file:

diffcone discover --rev HEAD --discover pytest --source-root src --source-root . -o targets.json

For pytest, discovery follows each test's fixtures, so a change to a fixture or a conftest.py selects the tests that use it. Fixtures from well-known plugins (mocker, httpx_mock, freezer, benchmark and others) are recognised automatically. If your tests use fixtures from another installed plugin, name them with --assume-external-fixture NAME; otherwise diffcone can't see what they depend on and selects their tests every time.

When the plan exits with code 3

Exit code 3 means your runner may collect tests that diffcone can't see: for example a pytest plugin that collects classes by its own naming rules, or a test base class outside your source roots. The report's discovery section lists each case. Running only the selected tests could skip some, so diffcone run refuses unless you pass --allow-incomplete-discovery. See static discovery.

items.title: List them in a manifest
items.text: For a runner without discovery, or to adjust what discovery finds, pass a target manifest with --targets targets.json. You can combine it with --discover; manifest entries replace discovered targets with the same ID.

items.title: Declare dependencies diffcone can't see
items.text:
Some dependencies aren't visible in the code: a plugin registered through entry points, a handler named in a configuration file. Declare them in a diffcone.toml at the repository root:

[[edges]]
from = "pkg.registry.dispatch"
to = "pkg.handlers.json_handler"
why = "handlers register themselves through entry points"

Now a change to json_handler selects the tests that reach dispatch.

Tests you want on every pull request whatever it changes, such as an end-to-end suite, go in the same file:

[[always_run]]
targets = "tests/e2e/*"

See the diffcone.toml reference.

items.title: Speed
items.text:
diffcone caches its analysis in .diffcone/cache/ (add .diffcone/ to your .gitignore). Committed snapshots are analysed once, and every file is cached by its content, so planning your working tree again only re-reads the files you changed. Cached and uncached plans are identical, and so are the manifests diffcone discover writes, which uses the same cache.

  • --no-cache turns the cache off; --cache-dir moves it.
  • diffcone prune --keep HEAD removes everything the cache doesn't need for planning from a commit, which keeps a cache saved between CI runs small. Pass it the same --source-root options you plan with: it keeps only the entries for those roots.

items.title: Running and checking
items.text:
Planning never runs your code, with or without a recording. These commands run tests after a plan exists, using the command line you give them.

The examples use the default source root, the repository itself. For a src layout, add --source-root src --source-root . to each command, as in planning.

items.title: Run the selected tests
items.text:
diffcone run --base main --head WORKTREE --discover pytest \
    --command "uv run pytest" -- -x

run builds the same plan as diffcone plan, then runs only the selected tests. Everything after -- is passed to pytest. pytest collects your suite as usual and a small plugin keeps the selected tests, so conftests and plugins load exactly as in a full run. Tests pytest collects that the plan doesn't know about (from a plugin's own collection, for example) are kept too.

run exits with pytest's exit code, with two exceptions (see exit codes):

  • if a selected test wasn't collected and pytest otherwise succeeded, it exits 3, since the run may have skipped tests;
  • if nothing ran because nothing was selected, it exits 0.

Discovery reads the same pytest options the run will use: those after --, those written into --command (uv run pytest -p tests.plugin), and the PYTEST_ADDOPTS and PYTEST_PLUGINS environment variables. When you plan separately with diffcone plan, pass it the same --command and arguments, in the same environment. If discovery can't find pytest's arguments in --command (it looks for -m pytest or a pytest program, so a wrapper script is not recognised), the plan says so and exits 3.

If pytest didn't collect a selected test, the message also names any option among the effective pytest arguments that keeps tests out of a run by the cache or by name (--lf, --ff, --nf, --sw, -k, -m, --deselect) and where it is set, since that is the usual reason.

For ASV, --runner asv builds the matching asv run --bench pattern. Add --dry-run to print the command instead of running it:

diffcone run --base main --head HEAD --discover asv --runner asv --dry-run

For pytest, the printed command names the selected tests as node ids. It is close to, but not the same as, what run does:

  • it leaves out tests pytest collects that the plan doesn't know, which run keeps;
  • naming tests on the command line makes pytest load their conftest.py files earlier than a normal run does;
  • with --evidence, a dry run doesn't check the environment against the recording.

run refuses to start in two situations, each with an option to override:

  • The checkout differs from what was planned. If you planned a commit or INDEX and the working tree differs in a file the plan depends on, run refuses and names the files. That includes any file under your source roots, a git-ignored .py beside tracked code, any conftest.py, pytest or ASV configuration, diffcone.toml, dependency and lock files, and submodules. Plan with --head WORKTREE, or pass --allow-mismatched-worktree.
  • Discovery may be incomplete (exit code 3). Pass --allow-incomplete-discovery to run the selection anyway.

items.title: Check a plan against a full run
items.text:
To trust a selection, you want to know: did it select every test that failed? diffcone check answers that from the JUnit XML of a full test run. It doesn't run anything, so you can add it next to an existing CI job:

pytest --junitxml=full.xml
diffcone plan --base main --head HEAD --discover pytest -o plan.json
diffcone check --plan plan.json --full full.xml

It lists every test that failed or errored in the full run but wasn't selected, and exits with 1 if there is one. Options:

  • --full and --baseline can be repeated: several files (from a sharded or split run, say) count as one run.
  • --baseline base.xml takes a run from before the change. Tests that failed there too are reported as already failing, not as misses. Each parametrized case counts on its own: a case that failed at the baseline doesn't excuse a new failure of another case.
  • --run NAME=JUNIT adds a selective run to compare on the same failures: diffcone's own run of the plan, or another test-selection tool's. Name diffcone's own run diffcone (--run diffcone=diffcone.xml): a new failure it didn't execute is a miss too, even if the plan selected it.
  • --format markdown writes a summary table for a CI job summary, and --format json a report for scripts.

JUnit names tests relative to pytest's rootdir, sometimes with a --junit-prefix. The plan records both, so plan with the same --command and arguments as the run. If they differ, pass --rootdir DIR (relative to the repository) or --junit-prefix PREFIX. If no case matches a target at all, the report says so and points at these options, rather than reporting every failure as a miss.

A directory that fails to collect (its conftest.py doesn't import) counts as a collection failure of every test under it. It is caught when any of them was selected.

items.title: The JSON report
items.text:
diffcone check --format json writes:

Field Contents ok true when there is no miss and nothing in not_run. misses The new failures the plan didn't select. not_run New failures diffcone's own run (--run diffcone=...) didn't execute. plan status, discovery_incomplete, and how many targets there were and how many were selected. full_run cases, test_time, selected_test_time (the full run's time for the selected tests) and unmatched_cases (cases that match no target). mapping The rootdir and junit_prefix the names were mapped with, and a note when no case matched a target. failures Every failure of the full run: test, outcome, kind, selected and already_failing (it failed in the baseline too). kind is test, collection (a file that failed to collect) or unknown (it matches no target). runs Each --run: name, cases, test_time, targets_run, misses (new failures it didn't run) and disagreements (tests it ran that failed in one run but not the other).

items.title: Validate a plan by running everything
items.text:
diffcone validate runs your whole suite on both snapshots and reports any test whose result changed but wasn't selected:

diffcone validate --base main --head HEAD --discover pytest \
    --source-root src --source-root . --command "uv run pytest"

Commits are checked out into temporary worktrees; WORKTREE runs in place. With --coverage (which needs pytest-cov installed where your tests run), it also records which tests executed changed code, and reports any such test that wasn't selected.

A miss comes in two kinds:

  • MISSED: a target whose result changed (or that executed changed code) and that the plan did not select.
  • A test that is not a target at all, because discovery did not find it. If the plan says its discovery is incomplete (it exits 3, and diffcone run refuses it without --allow-incomplete-discovery), such tests are a gap the plan already reported, not a selection miss: validate lists them as "outside the target list (discovery incomplete: the plan exits 3)" and they do not fail the check. Coverage recall is then measured over the targets, with the other tests counted apart (recall 100% of targets; 1589 test(s) outside the target list). If the plan claims its discovery is complete, such a test is a discovery miss and is reported as MISSED (not a target).

validate exits 0 when nothing was missed and 1 when something was. In --format json, missed lists every miss (each with "target": true or false), outside_targets lists the changed tests that are not targets, and discovery_incomplete says whether those count as misses; counts and coverage.counts carry missed_targets and outside_targets as well.

The whole suite must run on both sides for the comparison to mean anything, so validate, corpus and collect add --maxfail=0 after your arguments, which overrides an -x or --maxfail in addopts or in the command. A suite that still stops early (a conftest.py that sets maxfail, a plugin that ends the session) reports outcomes for fewer tests than it collected; validate then refuses with exit code 2 instead of comparing.

diffcone corpus --range A..B validates every commit in a range and summarises the results: how many failures were missed and what share of tests each plan would have skipped, with tests outside an incomplete target list counted apart, as validate does; it exits 1 when a plan missed something or a commit could not be validated. It skips commits that change no .py file unless you pass --all-commits. Use --jobs N to validate several commits in parallel. Both commands take --evidence to validate plans made from a recording.

Tips for both commands:

  • Pass the source roots that contain your package, so the tests run against the checked-out code rather than an installed copy.
  • If --command uses a relative path (.venv/bin/python -m pytest), it is resolved against the current directory, then the repository.
  • A temporary checkout gets your repository's copy of each git-ignored Python module inside a package that the commit lacks, such as the _version.py that setuptools-scm or hatch-vcs generate, so the package can be imported. Ignored conftests and test files are not copied.
  • --setup-command runs a shell command in each temporary checkout before its tests, for whatever else a build generates (compiled extensions).
  • pytest's cache plugin runs with an empty cache of its own: a configured --lf or --ff doesn't narrow or reorder the suite, and your .pytest_cache is left alone. If the cache can't be moved there, the run is refused. Don't disable the plugin in --command (-p no:cacheprovider) when your configuration or plugins need it.

items.title: Commands
items.text: Every command and its options. diffcone <command> --help prints the same information. plan, run and discover take a snapshot (--base, --head, --rev) as a git revision, INDEX (your staged changes) or WORKTREE (the files on disk); validate and corpus run your suite, so they take a revision or WORKTREE; collect --rev takes a revision. A revision the repository does not have is an error that names it (and says so when the clone is shallow).

items.title: Exit codes
items.text:
plan and discover:

  • 0: plan produced, analysis complete.
  • 1: plan produced, but analysis errors (a file that does not parse, a source root with no Python file) forced selecting everything.
  • 2: no plan (bad arguments, an unreadable manifest, an unknown revision, or an internal error).
  • 3: plan produced, but discovery may be short of what the runner collects.

1 and 3 are opposite failures: 1 selects too much, 3 means the target list itself may be short, so running only the selected targets could skip tests. 3 wins when both apply. A manifest written by discover keeps its notes, so a plan made from it exits 3 as well.

run exits with the runner's own code (0 when nothing was selected, or with --dry-run; pytest's 5, no test ran, counts as 0), and with 3 when a selected test was not collected. It refuses with 2 when the working tree differs from the snapshot the plan analysed (unless --allow-mismatched-worktree) or --repo is not the top of a git repository, and with 3 when discovery may be incomplete (unless --allow-incomplete-discovery).

validate and corpus exit 0 when every outcome change was selected, 1 when some were missed, 2 on errors. A test that is not a target is not a miss when the plan said its discovery is incomplete (the plan's 3); it is reported apart. check exits 0 when every new failure of the full run was selected, 1 when the plan missed one, 2 when an input cannot be read. report exits 0 when the runs it read show no problem, 1 when they show one (a miss, a check that reached no verdict, a selected test pytest did not collect, an artifact it could not read), 2 on errors. collect, prune and evidence exit 0 on success (collect records whatever the suite's own results) and 2 on errors. An internal error exits 2 in every command.

items.title: diffcone plan
items.text:
Produce a selection plan between two snapshots (revisions, INDEX or WORKTREE).

Compare two snapshots and report which targets are affected. A snapshot is a git revision, INDEX (staged content) or WORKTREE (files on disk). The report states exactly which kind was read. Targets come from --targets, from --discover, or both. Project code is never executed.

diffcone plan [-h] --base BASE --head HEAD [--targets TARGETS] [--command COMMAND] [--repo REPO] [--source-root DIR[=PREFIX]] [--discover RUNNER] [--assume-external-fixture NAME] [--no-well-known-fixtures] [--output OUTPUT] [--no-cache] [--cache-dir CACHE_DIR] [--evidence auto|PATH] [--format {json,text}] [runner_args ...]
Option Default Description --base BASE Required. Base snapshot: a git revision, INDEX or WORKTREE. --head HEAD Required. Head snapshot: a git revision, INDEX (staged content) or WORKTREE (files on disk, ignored files excluded). --targets TARGETS Path to a JSON target manifest. --command COMMAND The pytest command line the run will use: pytest options written in it (uv run pytest -p plugins.x) are read by discovery, as run reads them. --repo REPO . Path to the git repository (default: .). --source-root DIR[=PREFIX] Repo-relative directory whose .py files are analyzed as a module tree (repeatable; overrides the manifest's source_roots; default: .). DIR=PREFIX names its modules PREFIX.<path>, for per-package test trees whose files share names. --discover RUNNER Statically discover targets for a runner (pytest, asv); repeatable. One of pytest, asv. --assume-external-fixture NAME Pytest fixture provided by an installed plugin; not reported as unresolved (fixtures of well-known plugins such as pytest-mock's mocker are assumed by default). Repeatable. --no-well-known-fixtures Do not assume fixtures of well-known pytest plugins; report them as unresolved. --output, -o OUTPUT Write the result to this file instead of stdout (run: the command with --dry-run, otherwise the plan that ran, as plan writes it in JSON). --no-cache Do not read or write the cache (<repo>/.diffcone/cache): whole indexes and discovery results of committed snapshots, and per-module results, which also serve WORKTREE and INDEX. --cache-dir CACHE_DIR Where to keep the cache (default: <repo>/.diffcone/cache). --evidence auto|PATH Opt-in execution evidence (see diffcone collect): select pytest targets on what each test executed when recorded. auto picks the recording at the nearest ancestor commit; other runners' targets are planned statically. --format FORMAT json One of json, text. runner_args ... (after --) Pytest arguments the run will use (after --): options that change what pytest collects, such as --doctest-modules, are read by discovery.

items.title: diffcone run
items.text:
Plan, then execute only the selected targets with the runner's CLI.

Build a plan exactly like plan, then invoke the runner on the selected targets (pytest node ids, or an asv --bench pattern). Nothing is executed during analysis. Arguments after -- are passed to the runner.

diffcone run [-h] --base BASE --head HEAD [--targets TARGETS] [--runner {pytest,asv}] [--command COMMAND] [--dry-run] [--allow-mismatched-worktree] [--allow-incomplete-discovery] [--repo REPO] [--source-root DIR[=PREFIX]] [--discover RUNNER] [--assume-external-fixture NAME] [--no-well-known-fixtures] [--output OUTPUT] [--no-cache] [--cache-dir CACHE_DIR] [--evidence auto|PATH] [--collect] [runner_args ...]
Option Default Description --base BASE Required. Base snapshot: a git revision, INDEX or WORKTREE. --head HEAD Required. Head snapshot: a git revision, INDEX or WORKTREE. --targets TARGETS Path to a JSON target manifest. --runner RUNNER pytest Which runner to execute. One of pytest, asv. --command COMMAND Runner command line (default: "python -m pytest", or "asv run --python=same", which benchmarks the checkout in the current environment); run in --repo. --dry-run Print the command instead of running. --allow-mismatched-worktree Run even when the checkout is not the snapshot the plan analysed. --allow-incomplete-discovery Run even when discovery reports tests the runner may collect that are not targets. --repo REPO . Path to the git repository (default: .). --source-root DIR[=PREFIX] Repo-relative directory whose .py files are analyzed as a module tree (repeatable; overrides the manifest's source_roots; default: .). items.title: diffcone validate
items.text:
Run the full pytest suite at both snapshots and check the plan against it.

Outcome-based validation: runs the whole pytest suite at base and head (commits in temporary git worktrees, WORKTREE in place), then reports every test whose pass/fail outcome changed but was not selected. A test that is not a target is reported apart, not as a miss, when the plan says its discovery is incomplete. Behaviour changes that keep the same outcome are invisible to this check.

items.title: diffcone collect
items.text:
Run the whole pytest suite under the evidence recorder and store what each test executed.

Execution evidence (opt-in): run the whole suite once with diffcone's recorder (Python 3.12+) and write .diffcone/evidence/-.sqlite: the symbols each test executed and the repository files it touched, at a commit. Without --rev the repository itself runs and must be clean. Arguments after -- are passed to pytest. 

diffcone collect [-h] [--repo REPO] [--source-root DIR[=PREFIX]] [--rev REV] [--command COMMAND] [--setup-command SETUP_COMMAND] [--reverse-check] [--env-var NAME] [--no-cache] [--cache-dir CACHE_DIR] [runner_args ...]
Option Default Description --repo REPO . Path to the git repository (default: .). --source-root DIR[=PREFIX] As for plan (repeatable; default: .). --rev REV Collect at this commit, in a temporary worktree (default: the clean HEAD). --command COMMAND Pytest command line (default: "python -m pytest"). --setup-command SETUP_COMMAND Shell command run inside the temporary checkout (with --rev). --reverse-check Run the suite a second time in reverse order; tests whose records differ are marked unstable and always selected. --env-var NAME An environment variable that changes what tests do (a feature flag, say): recorded with the environment, and a run where it differs uses no evidence (repeatable). --no-cache Do not use the index cache. --cache-dir CACHE_DIR Where to keep the cache (default: <repo>/.diffcone/cache). runner_args ... (after --) Extra pytest arguments (after --).

items.title: diffcone check
items.text:
Check a plan against a full run's JUnit XML: was every failing test selected?

Read a plan (diffcone plan --format json) and the JUnit XML of a full pytest run, and report every test that failed or errored there but was not selected. A failure the --baseline run also had is reported as already failing. Each --run is a selective run (diffcone's own, or another selector's such as pytest-testmon) compared on the same failures. Runs nothing.

diffcone check [-h] --plan PLAN --full JUNIT [--baseline JUNIT] [--run NAME=JUNIT] [--rootdir DIR] [--junit-prefix PREFIX] [--format {text,markdown,json}] [--output OUTPUT]
Option Default Description --plan PLAN Required. The plan, as JSON. --full JUNIT Required. JUnit XML of the full run (repeatable: several files are one run). --baseline JUNIT JUnit XML of a run without the change (e.g. the nightly run at the evidence commit): its failures are not misses. Repeatable. --run NAME=JUNIT JUnit XML of a selective run to compare (repeatable). --rootdir DIR Pytest's rootdir, relative to the repository, which the JUnit names are relative to (default: the one the plan's discovery determined). --junit-prefix PREFIX The --junit-prefix the runs were made with (default: the one in the plan's pytest arguments). --format FORMAT text One of text, markdown, json. --output, -o OUTPUT Write the result to this file instead of stdout.

items.title: diffcone report
items.text:
Report on many CI runs of the diffcone actions: selection, checks, misses.

Read the results the run and record actions uploaded, downloaded into one directory per workflow run (DIR//run.json and DIR///), and report per job: the share pull requests selected and why some were planned from the code, and for pushes whether each was checked, its new failures, flaky re-runs and confirmed misses. The report action downloads the directory. Runs nothing. 

diffcone report [-h] --dir DIR [--format {markdown,json}] [--output OUTPUT]
Option Default Description --dir DIR Required. The directory of downloaded runs. --format FORMAT markdown One of markdown, json. --output, -o OUTPUT Write the report to this file instead of stdout.

items.title: diffcone prune
items.text:
Shrink the cache to what planning at given commits reads.

Delete every cached index and discovery result except those of the --keep commits, and every per-module record except those of their files (which also serve later commits and the working tree sharing them). For a cache shipped between CI runs: keep the commit the evidence was recorded at.

diffcone prune [-h] [--repo REPO] --keep REV [--source-root DIR[=PREFIX]] [--cache-dir CACHE_DIR]
Option Default Description --repo REPO . Path to the git repository (default: .). --keep REV Required. Commit to keep (repeatable). --source-root DIR[=PREFIX] The roots you plan with (repeatable; default: .); entries for other roots are deleted. --cache-dir CACHE_DIR The cache (default: <repo>/.diffcone/cache).

items.title: diffcone evidence
items.text:
List the evidence recordings of a repository.

diffcone evidence [-h] [--repo REPO]
Option Default Description --repo REPO . Path to the git repository (default: .).
