items.title: diffcone.toml
items.text:
Some dependencies can't be seen in the code: a plugin registered through entry points, a handler named in a configuration file, a registry filled when a module is imported. Declare them in a diffcone.toml file at the root of your repository:

[[edges]]
from = "pkg.registry.dispatch"
to = "pkg.handlers.json_handler"
why = "handlers register themselves through entry points"

[[edges]]
from = "pkg.cli"
to = "pkg.plugins"

Each [[edges]] entry says that from depends on to. A change to to then selects every target that reaches from, and the report explains the selection with your why.

Key Description from Required. The code that depends on something: a function, method, class or module, by its import path. A class or module includes everything defined in it, and a package its submodules. to Required. What it depends on, named the same way. why Optional. A short explanation, shown in the report.

items.title: Tests to run on every change
items.text:
Some tests are worth running on every pull request whatever it changes: an end-to-end suite, tests that drive the whole product. Name them with [[always_run]]:

[[always_run]]
targets = "tests/e2e/*"
why = "end to end"

[[always_run]]
targets = "*.TimeSuite.*"
runner = "asv"

Every target an entry matches is selected in every plan, and the report gives the entry as the reason.

Key Description targets Required. A pattern on the target's id, as the report shows it (tests/e2e/test_flow.py::test_login, bench_io.TimeRead.time_csv). * matches any characters, / and :: included; ? and [...] work as in shell patterns. runner Optional. Only this runner's targets: pytest, asv, or a runner your manifest's targets use. Any other name is an error. why Optional. A short explanation, shown in the report.

The tests still run when diffcone records a full run (diffcone collect), so the run that records evidence still tests them.

The report shows how many targets each entry matched. An entry whose pattern matches nothing isn't an error, because one diffcone.toml serves every job and a job may skip the directory an entry names; the text report flags it with MATCHES NOTHING, and the JSON report gives "matched": 0. diffcone can't tell a mistyped pattern (test/e2e/*) from one a job legitimately skips, so check the count when you add an entry or move tests.

items.title: Files to leave out of the analysis
items.text:
Some projects keep .py files that are not meant to be imported, and some of them are not even valid Python: test cases for a formatter or a linter, say. diffcone can't analyse such a file, so every plan selects every test, and diffcone collect refuses to record. List them under [index]:

[index]
exclude = ["tests/data/**"]
Key Description exclude A list of patterns on file paths from the repository root. * matches any characters, / included; ? and [...] work as in shell patterns.

A .py file that matches is treated like any other file diffcone doesn't analyse, a data file, say. A change to it makes a plan without a recording select every test. With a recording, it selects the tests that read the file or ran its code. The report lists each snapshot's patterns (analysis.base.excluded, analysis.head.excluded).

Don't exclude a file pytest collects tests from, or a conftest.py: its tests can't be targets, so the plan says discovery is incomplete, and the tests under an excluded conftest.py are always selected.

items.title: What can go wrong
items.text:
Declarations can only add dependencies or selected tests, so they can only make diffcone select more tests, never fewer.

diffcone reads the file from both snapshots, so it changes along with your code. These are reported as an analysis error:

  • a declaration that names something that doesn't exist;
  • an always_run entry without targets, or with an unknown runner;
  • an [index] table that isn't a table, or an exclude that isn't a list of non-empty patterns;
  • an unknown key;
  • a file that doesn't parse;
  • a file that is there but can't be read (left unmerged by a conflicted merge, say);
  • a declaration between two very large modules (more than 5,000 pairs of symbols): declare the specific functions instead.

An analysis error makes the plan select every target, so these mistakes can't silently remove tests from a plan. The one mistake diffcone can't catch is an always_run pattern that matches nothing (see above): the plan stands, and only the count shows it.

items.title: Static discovery
items.text: --discover pytest and --discover asv find targets by reading your configuration and test files, without importing them. This page lists what each one understands.

items.title: pytest
items.text:
Configuration is read from pytest.toml, .pytest.toml, pytest.ini, .pytest.ini, pyproject.toml ([tool.pytest.ini_options] or [tool.pytest]), tox.ini or setup.cfg at the root of the repository, in pytest's order: testpaths, python_files, python_classes, python_functions, norecursedirs, usefixtures, and the options in addopts. pytest reads options from three more places, and so does discovery, in pytest's order: the PYTEST_ADDOPTS environment variable, the pytest arguments written into --command (uv run pytest -p tests.plugin), and the arguments you pass after --. Plugins named in PYTEST_PLUGINS are loaded too.

Planning reads the environment when it runs, so plan in the environment the tests run in. The report's discovery section lists what it read (run_arguments), and pytest's rootdir, configfile and --junit-prefix (junit_prefix) as they follow from the configuration and arguments; diffcone check uses those to match JUnit names to tests.

Among those options:

  • test files or directories (. included) replace testpaths, as they do for pytest; a .txt or .rst file named there is a doctest;
  • --ignore and --ignore-glob leave paths out, and norecursedirs skips directories, below the paths pytest starts from, never those paths themselves; a pytest_ignore_collect hook in a conftest.py that can return False overrides both under its directory, so they are not applied there;
  • -o name=value overrides the configuration (-o addopts= drops the configured addopts);
  • an absolute path inside the repository counts as the relative one.

Tests found:

  • test functions and methods, following your naming settings;
  • test classes (without an __init__, unless they are unittest.TestCase subclasses), including nested classes and nested classes inherited from a base class;
  • unittest.TestCase subclasses, whatever their names;
  • tests inherited from base classes, including base classes in other modules;
  • tests imported into a test module, by name or with from module import *, including tests the other module imported itself or defines inside an if or try block;
  • tests bound to another name (test_alias = test_orig, also inside an if block), runTest in a unittest.TestCase without test* methods, and functions marked __test__ = True;
  • doctests: text files matching --doctest-glob (by default test*.txt), and the docstrings in your modules when --doctest-modules is set.

What each test depends on, besides its own code:

  • its fixtures, and the fixtures those use:
    • A fixture is requested by parameter, by usefixtures (the mark or the configuration option) or by request.getfixturevalue (every fixture the test can see, when the name isn't written out).
    • It is looked up the way pytest does: the class (including fixtures inherited from base classes in other modules), the module, each conftest.py outward, then plugins. Plugins are those listed in pytest_plugins (in any conftest or test module, and the plugins those list) and the pytest plugins of your project and of other packages in the repository. A pytest_plugins list may be built with +, +=, .append or .extend, or imported from another module.
    • A fixture is found under every name a module binds it to, as in pytest: an alias (box2 = box), an import (from tests.helpers import engine, from tests.helpers import *, through any number of modules) or a module attribute (engine = tests.helpers.engine), unless the fixture sets its own name=. When two plugins define a fixture of the same name, both count.
    • A name the test parametrizes is a parameter, not a fixture, for the test and for every fixture it uses, unless indirect hands it to the fixture. When indirect is a variable rather than True, False or a list of names, every name that has a fixture counts as handed over.
  • for a test that uses pytester or testdir, every fixture of the session's plugins (entry points, -p, PYTEST_PLUGINS, pytest_plugins): the pytest session it runs loads them, and its inline test code may request any of them. What that inline code imports is followed too;
  • marks such as usefixtures and parametrize on its class and the class's base classes, including marks stored in a variable and applied by name (needs_db = pytest.mark.usefixtures("db"), then @needs_db), and pytestmark lists built with +, +=, .append or .extend;
  • autouse fixtures that apply to it, including ones whose autouse= is a variable and ones a conftest.py, test module or plugin imports;
  • xunit-style setup_* and teardown_* functions, and unittest's setUpModule, setUp, asyncSetUp, setUpClass and their teardowns;
  • its module, and every conftest.py on its path with their pytest_* hooks, including hooks they import;
  • hooks that run for the whole session, such as pytest_collection_modifyitems and pytest_configure, in any conftest.py pytest loads (including the one in a test* directory of a path pytest starts from, which it loads even when that directory is ignored) and in your plugins;
  • your plugins' modules, which load for the whole session;
  • the pytest_* methods of any class in your source roots, since pytest calls them for every test once the class is registered as a plugin (config.pluginmanager.register(MyPlugin())), and the hooks of a module registered by name (config.pluginmanager.import_plugin( "tests.plugin"));
  • code pytest runs while it collects, before any test, that changes the process for every test after it: a conftest.py, a test module or a module they import that sets an environment variable or extends sys.path when imported, or a pytest_generate_tests in a sub-directory's conftest.py that does (see below for what counts).

Changes to the process that diffcone recognises:

  • writes to os.environ, sys.path and sys.modules;
  • attributes set on third-party modules;
  • common configuration calls such as warnings.filterwarnings, logging.basicConfig, locale.setlocale, numpy.random.seed and hypothesis's settings.load_profile.

They count whether made directly or through a patch that is not undone when a test ends (mock.patch.dict(os.environ, ...).start(), pytest.MonkeyPatch().setenv(...)). State a library keeps behind its own configuration function is not recognised; declare such a dependency in diffcone.toml if a test relies on it.

A test is also selected when what runs around it changes although its own code did not: for example, a test module adds a plugin to pytest_plugins, whose autouse fixture then applies to every test.

A doctest depends on everything its module can reach, and on the fixtures pytest gives it: autouse fixtures (such as one that fills doctest_namespace) and the usefixtures option. A doctest in a text file is always selected.

A conftest.py outside your source roots can't be read, so the tests under it are always selected and the report says why; add a source root that contains it. The same goes for a plugin in your repository that your source roots don't hold (pytest_plugins = ["support.plugin"] with support/ outside them): every test is always selected. And when diffcone can't read which plugins pytest_plugins names (it is built by a function call or a comprehension, or imported from outside your source roots), every test is always selected too; write the list out as strings to avoid that.

Some files can change what any test does, so a change to one selects every target. Outside your source roots, these are:

  • your runner configuration or build script: pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, setup.py, noxfile.py, hatch.toml, a conftest.py, asv.conf.json or asv.conf.jsonc;
  • your dependencies: a lock file such as uv.lock, any file or directory named for requirements, constraints or deps (dev-requirements.txt, ci/deps/py311.yaml), a conda environment*.yml, and installed package metadata (a *.dist-info or *.egg-info directory);
  • your CI configuration (.github/workflows/, ci/);
  • a .env or .pth file, or sitecustomize.py;
  • a type checker or linter configuration that a pytest plugin may run (mypy.ini, ruff.toml);
  • compiled sources.

Inside your source roots, a change to any file that isn't a .py file selects every target: a data file, a README.md, a configuration file. So does a change to a file's mode (a script made executable), and a change to a build script or sitecustomize.py, wherever it sits. diffcone.toml and .diffcone/ are the exceptions. With the source root ., every file in the repository is under a root (see limitations).

Other files outside the roots are assumed not to affect the tests: if your tests read one, put it under a source root.

items.title: Fixtures from installed plugins
items.text:
A fixture that isn't defined in your source roots usually comes from an installed plugin. diffcone recognises the fixtures of well-known plugins (mocker, httpx_mock, freezer, anyio_backend, benchmark and others), and lists each one it assumes in the report. Name fixtures from other plugins with --assume-external-fixture NAME. A fixture diffcone can't find otherwise is reported, and the tests that use it are selected on every change, since diffcone can't tell what the fixture depends on.

A fixture is a function under a decorator whose name ends in fixture: pytest.fixture, pytest-asyncio's fixture, pytest-twisted's async_fixture and async_yield_fixture, pytest-trio's trio_fixture. A plugin's fixture name is assumed only when nothing your tests can see defines it. If a test class, test module, conftest or plugin module defines that name under some other decorator, or binds it to something diffcone can't read (client = make_fixture(...)), diffcone treats it as an unknown fixture instead, and selects the tests that use it on every change.

Some fixtures are requested by pytest or a plugin itself rather than by your tests: pytest's tmp_path uses tmp_path_factory, and anyio's plugin uses anyio_backend. If your project overrides one, diffcone counts the override as a dependency of the tests that use it: for pytest's fixtures, the tests that use the fixture requesting it; for a plugin's, every test that can see the override.

items.title: Parametrized tests
items.text: Each test is a single target: diffcone selects or skips all of its parameter cases together.

items.title: ASV
items.text:
• Where. benchmark_dir is read from asv.conf.json or asv.conf.jsonc: the one nearest the root of the repository, up to three levels down. Comments and trailing commas are allowed. The directory is relative to the one holding the file ("." is that directory itself), and defaults to benchmarks.
  • Benchmarks. Functions and methods whose names start with time_, timeraw_, mem_, peakmem_ or track_ (or Time, Timeraw, Mem, PeakMem, Track followed by a capital or an underscore), in every module under benchmark_dir as ASV walks it. Inherited ones and ones imported into a benchmark module count. They are named as ASV names them; a benchmark_name you set is used, also for the function imported elsewhere or inherited by a subclass.
  • What each depends on. Its module and class (class attributes such as params count as part of the class), and:
    • its class's and module's setup, setup_cache and teardown, also when imported from another module (setup and teardown in any case, such as setUp, as ASV finds them);
    • the __init__, __new__, __getattr__ and __getattribute__ of its class, which ASV runs for every benchmark, also when inherited.
  • timeraw_ benchmarks (by the name ASV matches: timeraw_import = _impl is one) also depend on the modules their code imports. If the code isn't a plain string, the benchmark is always selected.

items.title: When the target list may be short
items.text:
Some things can't be known by reading the source:

  • a pytest plugin that collects tests by its own rules, such as classes with a different naming pattern;
  • a test base class, or an imported test, from outside your source roots;
  • an imported test that its module binds to something discovery can't follow (test_x = factory.make);
  • a test file, benchmark file or doctest module outside your source roots (with --source-root src, add --source-root . for tests in tests/), or a benchmark_dir outside the repository;
  • options that change what pytest collects in ways discovery doesn't follow (-c/--config-file, --rootdir, --pyargs), or a configuration file below the repository root that pytest will use (its rootdir is then that directory, the monorepo shape): discovery reads only the configuration at the root, so what the nested file sets is not known;
  • a --command discovery can't find pytest's arguments in (it looks for -m pytest or a pytest program), or one that names pytest more than once;
  • a path given to pytest that doesn't exist in the repository;
  • a plugin with a pytest_ignore_collect hook that can return False;
  • a conftest.py or plugin that turns files or objects into tests itself (pytest_collect_file, pytest_collect_directory, pytest_pycollect_makeitem), whether it defines the hook or imports it, and one that star-imports (from module import *) from outside your source roots, since that may bring such a hook in;
  • a --doctest-glob that matches files other than .txt, .rst or .md;
  • a test given by node id (tests/test_x.py::test_one), or a path right after an option that may take it as its value (--cov src), wherever pytest's arguments come from: addopts, PYTEST_ADDOPTS, --command or after --;
  • a test bound to something discovery can't follow (TestMachine = Machine.TestCase);
  • a plugin your configuration turns on that collects files of its own (pytest-typing's typing_checkers, --nbval, --markdown-docs);
  • a test file that can't be parsed;
  • a runner configuration file that can't be parsed (pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, asv.conf.json and the like): what it sets is unknown, so the defaults are used.

Each one appears as a note in the report's discovery section, and the plan exits with code 3: running only the selected tests could skip tests your runner would collect. You can:

  • widen your source roots so the missing code is analysed;
  • list the missing tests in a manifest; or
  • use execution evidence: a recording captures what pytest really collected, which can settle a note.

A recording settles a pytest note when pytest collected nothing at the recorded commit that wasn't a target, the same note stood there too, and the file it names is unchanged since. Notes about options, the command line or the configuration (an unparsable configuration file, a plugin the configuration turns on, an option or path discovery doesn't model) name no file, so a recording never settles them; nor does it settle ASV notes.

items.title: Target manifest
items.text:
A manifest lists targets explicitly. Use one for a runner that has no discovery, or to adjust what discovery finds. diffcone discover -o targets.json writes a manifest of the discovered targets, and --targets targets.json reads one.

{
  "source_roots": ["src", "."],
  "targets": [
    {
      "runner": "pytest",
      "runner_id": "tests/test_calc.py::test_add",
      "entry_symbol": "tests.test_calc.test_add",
      "lifecycle_dependencies": ["tests.conftest.db"]
    },
    {
      "runner": "asv",
      "runner_id": "bench_calc.TimeCalc.time_add",
      "entry_symbol": "benchmarks.bench_calc.TimeCalc.time_add",
      "lifecycle_dependencies": ["benchmarks.bench_calc.TimeCalc.setup"]
    }
  ]
}
Field Description source_roots Optional. The source roots the names below use, DIR=PREFIX included. --source-root overrides it. runner Which runner runs the target. diffcone run supports pytest and asv; other runners can be planned but not run. runner_id The name the runner uses for the target: a pytest node ID (without parameters) or an ASV benchmark name. entry_symbol The test or benchmark function, as an import path: module, then classes, then function. lifecycle_dependencies Code the runner runs for this target outside its own function: pytest fixtures, ASV setup and setup_cache, or a module (so module-level code such as pytestmark counts).

A manifest may also be just the list of targets, without the surrounding object. An unknown key, a missing field or the same target listed twice is an error, and the plan exits with code 2.

A manifest written by diffcone discover also has a discovery key with the notes discovery reported. Keep it: a manifest whose notes say the target list may be short makes the plan exit with code 3, as discovery itself would.

When you combine a manifest with --discover, a manifest entry replaces a discovered target with the same runner and runner_id.

A dependency written fixture:<name> marks a fixture whose definition couldn't be found. diffcone can't tell what such a fixture depends on, so it selects the target on every change.

items.title: Report
items.text: diffcone plan prints a JSON report (--format text prints a readable summary of the same information). The report's format is versioned by schema_version, currently 3.

items.title: Top-level fields
items.text: Field Contents schema_version The report format version, 3. status complete, or degraded when an analysis error made diffcone select every target. discovery_incomplete true when the runner may collect tests diffcone couldn't see; the plan then exits with code 3. analysis What was compared: both snapshots, the source roots, whether uncommitted files were analysed, counts, and the recording used, if any. changed_symbols Every symbol that differs between the snapshots. selected_targets The targets to run, and why. unselected_targets The targets not affected, and why. dependency_explanations For each selected target, the path from the target to the change. unresolved_relationships References diffcone couldn't resolve, and which changes they might reach. fallback_decisions Where diffcone selected more because it couldn't tell what a change reaches. analysis_errors Errors such as a file that doesn't parse. Any error selects every target. declarations The dependencies declared in diffcone.toml. always_run The [[always_run]] entries of diffcone.toml; each says how many targets it matched, and analysis.counts.always_run counts the targets they selected. discovery For each runner: how many targets were found, the configuration read, and any notes. For pytest, the configuration includes rootdir, configfile and junit_prefix (which diffcone check uses to match JUnit names), and run_arguments, what was read besides the configuration file: PYTEST_ADDOPTS, PYTEST_PLUGINS, the pytest arguments in --command and those after --.

items.title: Recording
items.text:
With a recording, analysis.evidence describes it:

Field Contents store The recording's path. commit The commit it was recorded at. environment_hash A hash of the recorded environment. environment_checked Whether this environment was checked against the recording (see below). python The recorded Python version. hash_seed The recorded PYTHONHASHSEED. variables The names of the environment variables it recorded. created When it was recorded, in seconds since the epoch. tests How many tests it holds. reverse_checked Whether it was recorded with --reverse-check. planned The plans made from it: from the recorded commit to each snapshot. changes_outside_range Changes made since the recording that lie outside base..head; they were planned too. escalated_modules Modules whose changes couldn't be judged from the recording and were planned from the code. preloaded_modules Modules of your project imported before the recorder started; changes to them are planned from the code.

plan can't check the environment, so it reports environment_checked: false: the selection holds only in the recorded environment. run checks it before any test runs, and its -o report says true when it matched.

The plan diffcone run -o writes is the plan that ran. When the run didn't use the recording because the environment differed, it also has evidence_not_used: reason (environment), differences (what differed, as run prints it) and recording_changed_its_environment (true when this environment is the one the recording's own test run started in, so the recorded tests changed it).

items.title: Snapshots
items.text:
analysis.base and analysis.head describe the two snapshots:

Field Contents revision What you asked for: main, HEAD~1, WORKTREE. commit The commit it resolved to (for INDEX and WORKTREE, the commit they sit on). kind commit, index or worktree. uncommitted true for INDEX and WORKTREE. description A readable summary, as the text report prints it. excluded The [index] exclude patterns of the snapshot's diffcone.toml (see diffcone.toml); empty when there are none.

items.title: Changed symbols
items.text:
{
  "id": "calc.ops.mul",
  "kind": "function",
  "changes": ["body_changed"],
  "base_path": "src/calc/ops.py",
  "head_path": "src/calc/ops.py"
}

changes lists one or more of added, deleted, body_changed, definition_changed, annotations_changed, dependencies_changed, dependencies_added, imports_added and docstring_changed (what they mean). imports_added and docstring_changed are listed for completeness. They select tests only where the new names or the docstring are used, or, for a new import, where a module that now runs (or no longer runs) on import registers or changes something the tests read.

items.title: Selected targets
items.text:
{
  "runner": "pytest",
  "runner_id": "tests/test_calc.py::test_square",
  "entry_symbol": "tests.test_calc.test_square",
  "lifecycle_dependencies": ["tests.test_calc"],
  "rules": ["dependency"],
  "conservative": false,
  "affected_dependencies": ["tests.test_calc.test_square"]
}

rules says how the target was selected. conservative is true when any of them is a fallback: something diffcone couldn't bound, so it selected the target to be safe.

Rule Fallback Meaning dependency A chain of calls, references or imports connects the target to a change (the target's own code included), shown in dependency_explanations. new_target The target is new. lifecycle_changed What runs around the target changed though its own code didn't: a fixture, hook or plugin now applies to it, or no longer does (another test module adds a plugin to pytest_plugins, for example). With a recording, compared with what ran around it when it was recorded. entry_docstring_changed The target's docstring changed; for a doctest, the docstring is the test. declared_dependency A dependency declared in diffcone.toml connects it to a change. always_run An [[always_run]] entry in diffcone.toml names it: it runs on every change. dynamic_reference yes It reaches code that looks names up dynamically (getattr, importlib), runs text built at run time as code, or runs a program it can't bound, and a change could be among what that reaches; or it runs with a module's globals (a doctest) and that module's imports changed. unresolved_name_match yes It reaches a reference diffcone couldn't resolve (a call, a name or an attribute) whose name matches something that changed. entry_symbol_unresolved yes Its own code wasn't found in either snapshot. lifecycle_dependency_unresolved yes Something it depends on wasn't found: a fixture diffcone couldn't find, a conftest.py or pytest plugin outside the source roots, a benchmark's code it couldn't read. analysis_error yes A file, or diffcone.toml, couldn't be analysed, so every target is selected. runner_dependency yes Code the test runner itself imports changed. unanalysed_file_changed yes A file diffcone doesn't read changed under the source roots (data, compiled sources, configuration), or a file's mode changed there (made executable, turned into a symlink). Or, outside the roots, your runner configuration, a conftest.py, a build script, dependencies or a lock file changed. For one target: a Python file it runs by path, which no module name maps to, changed.

With execution evidence, the rules name what the recorded run observed:

Rule Fallback Meaning executed_changed The test ran a changed function. executed_reader The test ran code that reads a changed value or definition, or reads a cache that code able to run changed code fills (an earlier test may have filled it, so the test never ran that code). The cache may be a module variable, or kept on an object, in a closure, in a function attribute or by a memoising decorator such as cached_property. touched_file The test read a file that changed. changed_target The test's own code, or its class or module, changed. test_scope Test code it shares a scope with changed (a mark, fixture or parameter). collection_code pytest ran changed code, or code that reads something that changed, while it collected the test's file in the recording (building parameter ids, an ids= function, pytest_generate_tests): that code decides the file's tests, their parameters, ids and marks. escalated The change can't be judged from a recording (code that runs on import, or a module imported before the recorder started), so it was planned from the code. cython_caller The test ran Cython code that calls a changed function the recording can't see. lookup_site yes The test looked a name up dynamically where something the lookup can see changed: a name added or removed, a definition or a value. no_evidence yes The test has no recording (a new test, for example), or it failed or errored while it was recorded, so its recording stops where it failed. unstable yes The test's recordings differed between runs. subprocess yes The test started a process the recording can't follow, or ran while one was still running. As a fallback for every test: such a process was started outside any test (a hook, collection, or an import outside the roots). text_code yes The test ran code compiled from text that no file of your code holds, such as a doctest's examples or a timeit statement: that code can use any name. pytest_hook_changed yes A pytest hook or what decides what pytest loads changed, or code that a hook ran in the recording (or that ran while pytest collected a file, and could change the whole process or pytest's session) changed or reads something that changed: what a hook does, such as setting an environment variable, reaches every test. unobserved_file_changed yes A change the recording can't attribute to tests: code that ran outside every test (a hook), a conftest.py outside the source roots, Cython outside functions or without a profiled build, other compiled sources, or your build, dependency or pytest configuration files. unindexed_import yes Changed code ran while a file outside the source roots was being imported, or such a file changed and was imported before the recorder started.

items.title: Exit codes
items.text:
Code Meaning 0 Plan produced; the analysis is complete. 1 Plan produced, but an analysis error made diffcone select every target. 2 No plan: a bad argument, an unreadable manifest, or an unknown revision. 3 Plan produced, but the runner may collect tests diffcone couldn't see.

When both 1 and 3 apply, the plan exits with 3.
